forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Woking's four-year audit backlog prevents finalization of recent accounts
news_drafts.lead: Woking Council faces a significant backlog of unfinalized accounts spanning 2019/20 to 2022/23 — four financial years — still incomplete after six years. The external auditor BDO has issued a disclaimed opinion for 2019/20, meaning the auditor cannot confirm whether the accounts are fairly stated, the most serious audit outcome. An unresolved objection to those accounts is blocking finalization, and BDO cannot guarantee amendments will not be required. Until this backlog is cleared, the successor auditor cannot finalize accounts from 2023/24 onwards. The committee heard the completion of 2019/20 would be "a significant milestone" in clearing this historic backlog.

news_drafts.headline: Woking council's £5.4m capital spending slips as homelessness costs pressure budget
news_drafts.lead: Woking council is forecasting that £5.4m of its approved capital spending will slip into future years, representing 15.6 per cent of the £34.8m programme for 2026-27. The slippage is distributed across the General Fund and the housing revenue account (HRA), the separate, ring-fenced account for the council's own housing stock. Simultaneously, the council's homelessness service is facing an ongoing cost pressure of £0.99m, driven by bed and breakfast expenditure for an average of 188 households — a figure that matches the five-year average, signalling a structural issue rather than temporary demand spike. The council's budget monitoring for the first quarter also identified a £1.42m shortfall from the budgeted sale of Albion House, and delays to essential works at Pool in the Park that are costing the leisure service £180k in lost management fee income.

findings.headline: Improvement and Recovery Programme forecast £1.64m favourable across 2025/26 and 2026/27 against an £8.4m budget
findings.detail: The 2026/27 forecast is £0.18m under budget, mainly from reprioritising projects to align with Local Government Reorganisation. Funding is £2.5m of flexible use of capital receipts and £5.9m from revenue budgets. All Q2 spend is forecast in revenue, and the relevant part will be capitalised at year end.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would compare the £2.5m of approved flexible use of capital receipts and the revenue-funded element with their own programme.
findings.quote: The total favourable forecast variance across the 2 years is £1.64m.

findings.headline: The approved 2026/27 budget includes £4.2m in savings and £3.2m in growth
findings.detail: The paper says the General Fund forecast includes the savings forecast and that work continues with budget holders to ensure savings targets are met. The savings tracker is listed as Appendix E, but its figures do not appear in this document, so achievement against the £4.2m is not shown. Appendix C records an unachieved £0.105m savings target on the HRA IT budget.
findings.matters: Savings delivery is the first thing a peer would check against an underspend, and this paper does not give the delivered share.
findings.quote: The approved budget includes £4.2m in savings and £3.2m growth.

findings.headline: Place and Digital favourable variance rises from £1.31m at Q1 to £1.74m at Q2
findings.detail: Digital Services is £625k favourable after budgets were identified as no longer needed following the Community Asset Transfer programme, updated agreements and licence renewals. Environmental Services is £769k favourable, largely from a higher ERP grant (£582k) than budgeted. Digital prepayments for next year reduce this year's forecast by £0.18m.
findings.matters: The favourable variance includes grant funding and prepayments for next year, which a reader would need to separate from ongoing savings.
findings.quote: the favourable variance of £1.31m at Q1 has improved to £1.74m at Q2

findings.headline: Sale of Albion House in March 2026 has resulted in £1.42m of unrealised budgeted income
findings.detail: The paper says the income loss is partly offset by reduced treasury financing costs. The Finance and Resources adverse variance narrowed from £1.80m at Q1 to £1.27m at Q2. The paper says income budgets affected by asset sales will be realigned.
findings.matters: Asset sales are removing income that councils budgeted against, and the paper says those budgets will be realigned.
findings.quote: has resulted in unrealised budgeted income of £1.42m

findings.headline: People and Communities adverse variance falls from £1.74m at Q1 to £0.37m at Q2, mainly from refreshed Homelessness forecasts (£0.86m)
findings.detail: Temporary accommodation is forecast £303k over budget, driven by repairs (£120k), utilities (£85k) and statutory expense (£73k). Homelessness overall is £233k favourable, from rental income and grants above budget. Leisure is £155k adverse, largely from lost income after WBC-commissioned flooring works at Pool in the Park overran.
findings.matters: Temporary accommodation and homelessness costs are demand-led, and the paper shows the forecast moving by £1.37m in one quarter.
findings.quote: the adverse variance of £1.74m in Q1 has reduced to £0.37m in Q2
